overview:
### cc-review CI integration — Difficulty: 3/5

This PR wires the external `cc-review` bot into the repo by adding three GitHub Actions workflows: an auto-review on PR open/push/label (`cc-review.yml`), an interactive `@cc-review` comment ping (`cc-review-interactive.yml`), and a cleanup job that deletes the ephemeral `pr-<N>-cc-review-output` log branch on PR close (`cc-review-cleanup.yml`). The shared pipeline is not vendored — each workflow mints a GitHub App token, clones the private `Questi0nM4rk/cc-review` repo at runtime with that token, and runs `scripts/ci-run.sh`, so the heavy logic updates centrally. Untrusted comment text is stripped of the `@cc-review` prefix and written to `/tmp/cc-user-msg.txt` as data rather than interpolated into a prompt, and the trigger gate parses `.cc-review.yaml` to decide whether to auto-run.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["PR event / comment / dispatch"] --> B{"which workflow?"}
  B -->|"PR opened / push / labeled"| C["cc-review.yml: resolve PR + read trigger from .cc-review.yaml"]
  B -->|"comment contains @cc-review"| D["cc-review-interactive.yml: extract msg to /tmp file"]
  B -->|"PR closed"| E["cc-review-cleanup.yml"]
  C --> F{"should_run? (trigger / label / dispatch)"}
  F -->|"false"| G["skip"]
  F -->|"true"| H["mint App token"]
  D --> H
  H --> I["clone private cc-review @ main with token"]
  I --> J["run scripts/ci-run.sh (CC_POST=1)"]
  J --> K["post review / walkthrough / status comment"]
  E --> L{"log branch exists?"}
  L -->|"yes"| M["gh api DELETE refs/heads/pr-N-cc-review-output"]
  L -->|"no"| N["nothing to delete"]
  class A,B,C,D,E,F,H,I,J,K,L,M chg
```

Riskiest area to watch: the runtime clone of a private repo using an App-token-embedded HTTPS URL plus execution of its `ci-run.sh` with secrets in env — supply-chain trust in `Questi0nM4rk/cc-review@main` and correct gating of untrusted comment bodies (which can run the pipeline on `issue_comment`) are the load-bearing concerns.

## Strict review

Inline comments mark required changes. Requesting changes until every thread is resolved.

<!-- cc-review:review fnv1a32:e5663a62 -->

comments.body:
Add an author-authorization gate to the `if:` condition before the privileged pipeline runs. As written, the condition only checks that the comment contains `@cc-review` and is attached to a PR; it does not check who posted it. The `issue_comment` event grants the base repository's full token context and this job mints a GitHub App token with `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, and `issues: write`, which is NOT downscoped for fork-originated PRs the way the default `pull_request` token is. Any external contributor who opened a PR from a fork can therefore comment `@cc-review` on their own PR and trigger the privileged pipeline (clone of the bot, write-scoped token, repo push access). Require `github.event.comment.author_association` to be one of `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, or `COLLABORATOR` (and exclude bot-authored comments) before the job runs.

<!-- cc-review:finding d776f8d8 -->

Verify — restrict the checkout/token combination for fork-originated PRs. The `pull_request` trigger checks out the PR head (`fetch-depth: 0`) of untrusted contributor code, and the same job mints a GitHub App token with `contents: write` / `pull-requests: write` / `issues: write` that — unlike the default fork `GITHUB_TOKEN` — retains write scope for fork PRs. The cloned `scripts/ci-run.sh` then runs against that checked-out tree with the write-scoped token in the environment, which is the classic pwn-request exposure: a fork PR can ship a malicious file (config, hook, script the pipeline reads) that runs with write access to the base repo. Gate the privileged path on the PR being non-fork or on author authorization, or run untrusted-checkout steps in a job that holds no write token.

<!-- cc-review:finding 7f86d12d -->

Verify — pin the runtime clone of the external `cc-review` repository to an immutable commit SHA rather than the mutable `main` branch (`-b "$CC_BOT_REF"` where `CC_BOT_REF: main`). Every consumer workflow run fetches and executes `scripts/ci-run.sh` from whatever `main` currently points to, with no review or pin gate; a forced-push or compromise of that branch immediately runs attacker-controlled code inside this repo's CI with the write-scoped App token and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the environment. Pin `CC_BOT_REF` to a specific commit SHA so the executed pipeline code cannot change underneath consumers without an explicit update.

<!-- cc-review:finding c624a831 -->

Verify — pin the runtime clone of the external `cc-review` repository to an immutable commit SHA rather than the mutable `main` branch (`-b "$CC_BOT_REF"`). Same mutable-ref supply-chain exposure as the clone step in cc-review.yml: the executed `scripts/ci-run.sh` is fetched from a moving branch and runs with the write-scoped App token and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` present. Pin to a commit SHA.

<!-- cc-review:finding 01fb5c92 -->

Fix the dead pipeline fallback in `TRIGGER=$(grep -oP '...' .cc-review.yaml 2>/dev/null | tr -d ... || echo "pr_open")`. The `|| echo "pr_open"` attaches to the pipeline's exit status, which is the exit status of the last stage (`tr`), not `grep`. `tr` always exits 0, so when `.cc-review.yaml` is absent or has no `trigger:` line, the fallback never fires and `TRIGGER` becomes the empty string (verified empirically). The intended default `pr_open` only survives because the next line's `[ -z "$TRIGGER" ] && TRIGGER="pr_open"` backstop catches it, making the `|| echo` here dead code. Remove the non-functional `|| echo "pr_open"` and rely on the `-z` backstop, or move the default into the grep stage so the fallback actually executes.

<!-- cc-review:finding 543f7353 -->
